title: Journeys Into Jazz radio show and WPEN record dubs
summary: Rose describes his radio series Journeys Into Jazz on WFIL in Philadelphia and recalls making dubs at WPEN.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: wouldn't exactly think of myself as a disc jockey. I did, of course, run the radio show Journeys Into Jazz, which began in 1946 in Philadelphia, and is now syndicated through Southern Illinois University Radio Network. And it's just a mini-series of programs about jazz and jazz musicians on which records are played for illustration. What station was this in Philadelphia? WFIL, ABC. They had a little Eastern network that covered a lot of ABC affiliates in the area, and I had a pretty big audience back in the 40s. What was WPEN? Was that station? WPEN was a radio station in Philadelphia too. I didn't do my show there, but I was a frequent guest on the station when they were the headquarters for the radio show called Jukebox Jury. I'm
trying to remember because it seemed to me that a few years ago we were looking at some copies of records. You made dubs. And the blanks came from WPEN. Could that be correct? Oh yes, because
they had the recording facilities to do it with. And they may have been records that I made up there with either Dan Burley or Fats Waller or Sammy Price. You recorded them? Yeah. I think
